title: Appliance repair marketing that connects searches to service calls
html:
A marketing plan built around the repairs you actually take

Wonderweb Studio helps appliance repair businesses connect search advertising, local visibility and a useful website with the people who answer their calls. We start with your accepted appliances, brands, service areas and dispatch capacity, then define the work in a written proposal. You can hire us for a focused channel or a connected marketing program.

A refrigerator that stopped cooling, a washer that will not drain and a restaurant looking for commercial equipment service are different inquiries. Your marketing should make those differences clear. A campaign that generates calls for appliances you do not repair is creating work for the office without helping the business.

Our team works remotely with U.S. businesses. Your real service territory shapes the campaign; a city mentioned in a plan does not imply a Wonderweb office there.

What our appliance repair marketing can include

We recommend the channels that fit the problem. A business missing useful search visibility needs a different scope from one receiving plenty of calls but losing them during intake.

Google Ads for the services you can fulfill

We organize search campaigns around the repair categories, coverage and hours agreed with you. Ad copy should make the service clear before someone clicks. We review search terms and inquiry outcomes together so irrelevant traffic can be addressed without blindly blocking valuable searches. See the appliance repair Google Ads guide for the channel-specific discussion.

Local SEO and useful service pages

We review important service pages, crawl access, business details and the links between related content. For an eligible Google Business Profile, we help keep the actual business and service-area information consistent. We do not create a profile at a virtual office for each city or claim that a map position can be purchased. Explore appliance repair SEO.

A website that helps a caller choose

The page should explain what you repair, where you travel, whether commercial work is accepted and what happens after contact. We review mobile usability, forms and phone links, and scope new website design or landing-page work when needed. Diagnostic fees, warranties and same-day availability appear only when your business can support those statements.

Choose repair inquiries that fit your team

Before choosing keywords, we document the jobs you want and the requests you cannot serve. Use the examples below as a brief, not a claim about your current service offering.

  • Do not advertise every appliance brand if the team services only selected brands.
  • Keep repair searches separate from parts sales, DIY instructions and employment inquiries.
  • Match call handling and ad schedules to the response process your office can maintain.
Inquiry typeWhat the page should explainWhat intake should confirm
Residential refrigerator repairAccepted brands, service area and how an assessment is arrangedZIP code, appliance type, symptom and contact details
Washer or dryer repairRepair versus installation scope and diagnostic processModel information if available and access constraints
Commercial appliance serviceThe equipment and business types you actually supportSite location, equipment, urgency and decision-maker
Warranty or manufacturer requestWhether your business is authorized to handle itCoverage requirements before an appointment is offered

Follow a lead from search to dispatch

A useful lead record links the marketing source to the actual request: appliance, location, contactability and the next action. Your dispatch team then records whether the request was accepted, an appointment was arranged, and the job was completed. A phone click alone cannot answer those questions.

For example, a homeowner searching for refrigerator repair may reach the right page but live outside your territory. That is different from a suitable caller who could not reach anyone. We use that distinction to decide whether to change targeting, page information or the handoff to your team.

Where the agreed tools support it, we configure inquiry tracking and a practical reporting view. Custom CRM work, call-tracking subscriptions and automation are scoped separately. The first goal is a trustworthy record of suitable inquiries, not a dashboard full of unqualified submissions.

What happens when we start working together

We agree on the priorities and responsibilities before campaign work begins. Timing depends on access, source material, approvals and the amount of website work needed.

First: map the business and the current gaps

We review your website, existing accounts, accepted jobs, coverage, intake process and available records. You identify the repair categories and capacity you want to prioritize. We document what can be reused and what needs attention.

Then: build the agreed inquiry path

We prepare the selected campaign or page work, confirm the message with you and test the contact path. An illustrative plan may start with one repair category and a focused territory, then expand after the response and measurement process is working.

Ongoing: review quality and choose the next change

We review available search terms, relevant visits and inquiry outcomes. You provide the service-side feedback that platforms cannot see. The next recommendation should explain what is changing and why it matters to your business.

How much does appliance repair marketing cost?

The price depends on the channels, service markets, website work and reporting requirements in your scope. Wonderweb’s connected monthly partnerships start at $3,000 USD; focused services and website projects have separate starting scopes. Compare the current pricing and inclusions before choosing a plan.

Advertising spend is separate from the management fee. Landing pages, creative production, tracking subscriptions and integrations may also be separate. Your written proposal identifies those costs so a low management headline does not hide the actual commitment.

To judge the test, compare acquisition cost with the economics of the jobs you accept. An inexpensive lead that cannot be served is not equivalent to a repair appointment. We agree on qualification and review criteria before interpreting the numbers.

A written lead commitment for eligible paid campaigns

If your eligible paid campaign misses its written qualified-lead target in its first 90 days, we provide 30 additional days of campaign management at no management fee. Your advertising spend remains separate.

Available for paid campaigns whose signed proposal includes this guarantee, a qualified-lead target and the agreed media budget before launch. The 90-day period begins when the campaign launches with working tracking.

A qualified lead is a genuine, new inquiry that matches the services and service area agreed in your proposal and includes usable contact information. Duplicate inquiries, spam, vendors and job seekers do not count. Any additional qualification criteria are agreed before launch.

You maintain the agreed advertising budget, provide required access and timely approvals, keep conversion tracking working and follow the response and lead-recording process in your proposal. The campaign and lead records must be available for the 90-day review.

If those conditions are met and the target is missed, the remedy is one additional 30-day management period for the covered campaign at no management fee. Media spend, third-party subscriptions and other services remain payable. This is a management-fee waiver, not an advertising refund or a promise of sales, revenue, rankings or platform approval.

Bring these five details to our first conversation

You do not need a finished marketing brief. These details give us enough context to discuss a useful next step.

  • Your website and the person who manages it.
  • The appliances, brands and customer types you accept.
  • Your actual service ZIP codes and dispatch capacity.
  • Your current advertising budget and account access, if applicable.
  • How calls and forms are handled, plus any lead records you already keep.

Primary references

  • Google Business Profile: represent your real business and service area
  • Google Ads: how Ad Rank affects eligibility and placement
